AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To analyze the prevalence of different degrees vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) in stroke and the characteristics of demography distribution in Inner Mongolia. In order to provide reference data and theoretical guidance for the prevention and treatment of VCI after stroke in the area.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Stratified multi-stage random sampling was used to extract 6 regions of Inner Mongolia as the first sampling cluster; and then the corresponding banners (counties) were selected randomly as the secondary sampling cluster; according to the number of patient required to investigation, the corresponding number of communities was randomly selected from the secondary sampling cluster. According to the diagnostic criteria of "Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of vascular cognitive impairment" and NINDS-AIREN, we screened all stroke patients aged 45 or older from each community, a total of 444 patients participated in the questionnaire and various scaleassessment.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The prevalence of VCI, VCIND and VD was 80.41%, 34.46% and 45.95% respectively. The prevalence of VCI in stroke was significantly different in different nationality, age and education level (P<0.05), and there was no significant difference in gender, occupation, marital status and family structure (P>0.05).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The prevalence of VCI after stroke was higher in Inner Mongolia, and VCI had a relatively high morbidity in old age people and person with less education in Chinese Han population.
